claim_limit: This map classifies current coupling. CORE_PORTABLE means the audited surface has no known Hermes implementation dependency; it does not by itself prove live multi-runtime behavioral parity.

classifications.CORE_PORTABLE: Runtime-neutral contract/logic with no known direct Hermes implementation dependency in the audited surface.
classifications.ADAPTER_BOUNDARY: Intentional boundary that knows about one or more runtime/provider interfaces but should keep runtime semantics outside portable core.
classifications.HERMES_SHAPED: A surface intended to participate in general product behavior but currently embeds Hermes-specific names, states, paths, lifecycle semantics, or assumptions.
classifications.RUNTIME_SPECIFIC_BY_DESIGN: A Hermes-specific distribution/integration surface whose runtime coupling is intentional and should remain behind an adapter or packaging boundary.
classifications.UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_PROOF: A mixed or insufficiently isolated surface; portability must not be claimed until coupling is split or executable evidence exists.

policy.direction_rule: portable core may define contracts used by adapters; portable core must not import Hermes implementation modules

surfaces.rationale: The source registry intentionally contains both portable worker semantics and runtime distribution preferences. lib/workforce.mjs now exposes an executable split: PORTABLE_WORKFORCE preserves identity, skills, governance and operational contracts while WORKFORCE_RUNTIME_PREFERENCES contains toolsets, optional integrations, distribution metadata and the source runtime-first memory hint.
surfaces.next_action: Keep new portable governance fields in the portable projection and keep runtime/distribution preferences isolated behind the explicit preferences map.

surfaces.rationale: Canonical skills now live under a runtime-neutral source root. Their compatibility metadata still requires adapter/export interpretation, so Chat 2 does not overclaim them as behaviorally portable.
surfaces.next_action: Keep runtime-specific activation in adapters/export targets; behavioral portability still requires live proof.

surfaces.rationale: Capability IDs, risk classes, connection truth and authorization routing are expressed independently of Hermes.
surfaces.next_action: Keep runtime capability realization behind adapters.

surfaces.rationale: Task lifecycle, approval and verification now bind to an opaque runtime provider/reference instead of hard-coding one runtime execution mode, task ID format, staging action or actor.
surfaces.next_action: Keep runtime-specific ID/reference construction in adapters; Chat 3 may consume this generic binding from an execution adapter.

surfaces.rationale: Risk classes, owner-approval requirements, independent verification rules and fail-closed execution gates operate on the portable worker projection and opaque runtime provider bindings. Tests prove the same approval behavior with an arbitrary runtime provider rather than a Hermes-specific task mode.
surfaces.next_action: Keep provider identity opaque to approval semantics; runtime adapters may bind tasks but may not redefine owner approval authority.

surfaces.rationale: Receipt signing, binding, freshness, replay, evidence references and verification do not depend on Hermes implementation modules.
surfaces.next_action: Retain as core; Chat 9-10 will add implementation-independent verification evidence.

surfaces.rationale: Canonical memory layers, evidence requirements and promotion rules are runtime-neutral even though employee profile metadata separately contains Hermes-first wording.
surfaces.next_action: Keep core policy neutral; move runtime memory preferences out of employee core contract.

surfaces.rationale: The doctor intentionally knows concrete harness/provider commands and reports availability without making them core workforce semantics.
surfaces.next_action: Keep provider-specific probing at the boundary and prevent it from becoming worker policy.

surfaces.rationale: The read-only SDK defines normalized runtime snapshots and policy-constrained adapters. Hermes is one configured adapter policy, not the only interface.
surfaces.next_action: Keep v1 read-only. Execution now uses the separate runtime-execution-adapter contract.

surfaces.rationale: Executable resolution, profile inspection, kanban invocation and Hermes environment rules are intentionally Hermes-specific.
surfaces.next_action: Keep behind a runtime-neutral office/runtime boundary.

surfaces.rationale: Profile installation, upgrade and Hermes-owned distribution layout are runtime packaging concerns.
surfaces.next_action: Retain as Hermes distribution implementation; do not leak lifecycle semantics into core.

surfaces.rationale: This boundary knows Hermes, Codex, Gemini and Copilot invocation/export details and already states that self-test success is not broad behavioral portability.
surfaces.next_action: Reuse its bounded harness knowledge for reference-case proof without promoting self-test to canonical live parity.

surfaces.rationale: Server and reconciliation consume a generic runtime provider shape. Hermes construction moved into the explicit composition root while the existing Hermes read-only adapter remains runtime-specific.
surfaces.next_action: Add execution-capable adapters separately without widening the read-only snapshot contract.

surfaces.rationale: The product installer now separates a runtime-neutral immutable core release channel from runtime-specific employee/profile lifecycle work. Stable source installation resolves tagged release assets, verifies manifest + SHA-256 + exact source commit, records provenance, and has no mutable-main fallback. Hermes profile install/upgrade/remove remains an explicit runtime boundary implemented by Hermes bootstrap/removal tooling rather than core source acquisition.
surfaces.next_action: Keep stable core acquisition runtime-neutral and fail-closed. Keep Hermes profile bootstrap/removal as runtime-specific distribution behavior; do not fold runtime profile lifecycle back into the stable source installer contract.

surfaces.rationale: Current employee release packs package Hermes profile distributions. They are valid release artifacts but are not a runtime-neutral worker package proof.
surfaces.next_action: Keep Hermes packs stable while defining portable core inputs separately.

surfaces.rationale: Real-task collection, hash-chain truth and evaluation readiness operate on evidence/task contracts rather than Hermes implementation details.
surfaces.next_action: Keep as core evidence machinery; do not require 20/20 for the v0.5 portability reference case.

surfaces.rationale: Release-claim construction and historical deferred-evidence semantics now share one provider-neutral package boundary under packages/release-claims. Historical v0.4 Hermes/provider evidence remains data, while synthetic-provider tests independently demonstrate that the claims model itself is provider-neutral.
surfaces.next_action: Keep historical release data truthful and runtime-specific as data; keep the consolidated release-claims evaluation/deferral logic provider-neutral.

surfaces.rationale: The office now consumes a portable WORKFORCE_VIEW for identity, governance and task ownership. Runtime toolsets, optional integrations, distribution metadata and source runtime-first memory hints are available only through an explicit runtime-preference map for labeled UI presentation.
surfaces.next_action: Keep runtime preference display optional and explicit; portable UI/task behavior must continue to use WORKFORCE_VIEW rather than the full generated distribution object.

surfaces.rationale: The generator still emits Hermes distributions by design, but canonical skill ownership is runtime-neutral and portable/core versus runtime distribution outputs are now separate responsibilities.
surfaces.next_action: Keep runtime distribution generation explicit; do not treat Hermes output generation as portable-core behavior.

surfaces.rationale: Portable worker projection strips runtime toolsets, optional integrations and distribution metadata while preserving identity, skills, governance and operational contracts.
surfaces.next_action: Use PORTABLE_WORKFORCE for runtime-neutral core and portability hashes; keep full WORKFORCE only where runtime packaging or UI compatibility needs it.

surfaces.rationale: A separately scoped fail-closed execution contract provides bounded prepare/execute/normalize/evidence/cleanup semantics without widening the read-only Runtime Adapter SDK.
surfaces.next_action: Implement Hermes and Codex reference adapters against this contract, then collect reference-case and live-runtime evidence before any portability promotion.

surfaces.rationale: The Siti reference worker projection, exact task, five canonical skills, READ_ONLY execution policy, source artifact, expected result, verification contract, and evidence expectations are hashed into one runtime-neutral core bundle. Runtime adapter/provider metadata is explicitly outside the core hash.
surfaces.next_action: Hermes and Codex execution adapters must consume this exact core bundle hash unchanged. Any drift blocks reference-case portability evidence.

surfaces.rationale: Hermes-specific one-shot execution is isolated behind RuntimeExecutionAdapter v1 and bound to the re-baselined canonical Siti core bundle. Portable worker identity is independent from the local Hermes runtime profile; the adapter defaults to the safe local `default` profile, exposes only the skills toolset, and ignores runtime rules that could replace the canonical worker contract.
surfaces.next_action: Run the separately authorized live Hermes reference case under the reviewed 45-second canonical execution policy; runtime profile/auth remains adapter metadata and must not alter the re-baselined core bundle.

surfaces.rationale: Codex-specific ephemeral read-only execution is isolated behind RuntimeExecutionAdapter v1, bound to the re-baselined canonical Siti bundle, stages the five canonical skills under .agents/skills, and ignores user config/rules so local configuration cannot silently change the reference case while authentication remains available.
surfaces.next_action: Run the bounded live Codex reference case under the reviewed 45-second canonical execution policy. This timeout was re-baselined from measured runtime latency and is part of the new core hash; do not promote partial/timeout attempts.

surfaces.rationale: Runtime-neutral comparator checks canonical core identity, Hermes+Codex runtime pairing, evidence completeness, protected expected atoms, prohibited-action/workspace state, exact live commit binding, and independent verification state before allowing a reference-case portability claim.
surfaces.next_action: Feed separately collected live Hermes/Codex run records into this comparator. Fixture evidence must remain PARTIAL and live evidence without independent verification must remain PORTABILITY_CANDIDATE.

surfaces.rationale: The harness binds canonical core plus runtime-specific adapters, provider detection, clean Git state and public-safety checks into redacted comparator-compatible run records while refusing fixture/provider-unverified promotion to LIVE_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE.
surfaces.next_action: Use explicit plan/run commands for separately authorized live Hermes and Codex reference attempts; keep generated records local until redaction/public review.

surfaces.rationale: Python independently verifies the signed receipt/evidence trust surface without importing or invoking the JavaScript verifier, providing a second implementation boundary for payload hash, Ed25519, bindings, freshness, replay, runtime scope, and receipt-reference checks.
surfaces.next_action: Build the shared adversarial differential corpus and require JavaScript/Python accept-reject agreement before claiming cross-implementation verification.

surfaces.rationale: One static signed-receipt corpus is consumed independently by the production JavaScript verifier and Python reference verifier; exact accept/reject, packet reason codes, receipt reason sets, and corpus SHA-256 must agree.
surfaces.next_action: Treat any future JavaScript/Python disagreement as a release-blocking contract regression; extend the corpus when the stable receipt trust surface changes.

surfaces.rationale: Public Ed25519 trust anchors, signer ownership, validity windows, runtime scope, ACTIVE/RETIRED/REVOKED lifecycle, explicit rotation overlap, and compromise policy are runtime-neutral receipt-governance semantics. Private signing material is explicitly forbidden from the registry.
surfaces.next_action: Populate deployment-specific public trust anchors only through reviewed release/configuration changes; keep private keys outside the repository and treat registry revocation as authoritative over legacy public-key maps.
